subproblem.title: Frame, dimension and pointwise distance bounds for the affine graph plane
subproblem.statement: Let n, k ∈ ℕ, T an n-dimensional linear subspace of ℝ^{n+k} (Module.finrank ℝ T = n), ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{n+k} linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 and ιv ∈ T for all v ∈ ℝⁿ, w ∈ ℝᵏ, Λ : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ continuous linear (operator norm ‖Λ‖), ξ ∈ ℝ^{n+k} and c ∈ ℝᵏ. Put τ := ξ + ι'c, L := ι + ι'∘Λ (Lean ι.toLinearMap + ι'.toLinearMap ∘ₗ Λ.toLinearMap), S := LinearMap.range L, and write p_S, p_T for the orthogonal projections onto S and T (Submodule.starProjection). Then: (a) dim S = n (Module.finrank ℝ S = n); (b) for all v ∈ ℝⁿ and w ∈ ℝᵏ, with y := (ξ + ιv + ι'w) − τ: |y − p_S y| ≤ |w − c − Λv| and |v| ≤ |y|; (c) for every x ∈ ℝ^{n+k}: |(x − τ) − p_S(x − τ)| ≤ |(x − ξ) − p_T(x − ξ)| + |c| + ‖Λ‖·|x − τ|.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n k : ℕ) (T : Submodule ℝ (Euclid (n + k))) (ι : Euclid n →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) (ι' : Euclid k →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) (Λ : Euclid n →L[ℝ] Euclid k) (ξ : Euclid (n + k)) (c : Euclid k), Module.finrank ℝ T = n → (∀ v w, inner ℝ (ι v) (ι' w) = 0) → (∀ v, ι v ∈ T) → Module.finrank ℝ (LinearMap.range (ι.toLinearMap + ι'.toLinearMap ∘ₗ Λ.toLinearMap)) = n ∧ (∀ (v : Euclid n) (w : Euclid k), ‖(ξ + ι v + ι' w - (ξ + ι' c)) - (LinearMap.range (ι.toLinearMap + ι'.toLinearMap ∘ₗ Λ.toLinearMap)).starProjection (ξ + ι v + ι' w - (ξ + ι' c))‖ ≤ ‖w - c - Λ v‖ ∧ ‖v‖ ≤ ‖ξ + ι v + ι' w - (ξ + ι' c)‖) ∧ ∀ x : Euclid (n + k), ‖(x - (ξ + ι' c)) - (LinearMap.range (ι.toLinearMap + ι'.toLinearMap ∘ₗ Λ.toLinearMap)).starProjection (x - (ξ + ι' c))‖ ≤ ‖(x - ξ) - T.starProjection (x - ξ)‖ + ‖c‖ + ‖Λ‖ * ‖x - (ξ + ι' c)‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 0–4 of the parent proof of dorag_tes_graph_affine_height. These formalize Simon, Ch. 5, proof of Theorem 4.5 (Tilt-excess Decay Theorem), book/chapter-05.txt lines 960–962: dist(x, τ + S) ≤ |f(x′) − λ(x′)| for x = (x′, f(x′)) ∈ B_{θρ}(τ) ∩ graph f. They also formalize the bound off graph f, which line 967 obtains from the height bound (2) (line 789) and (18) (line 943). Here the frame ℝ^{n+k} = range ι ⊕ range ι′, dim S = n, and these distance bounds are stated without the measure, the Lipschitz map f or the radius t.
1. (Pythagoras.) For v ∈ ℝⁿ and u ∈ ℝᵏ: |ιv + ι'u|² = |ιv|² + 2⟨ιv, ι'u⟩ + |ι'u|² = |v|² + |u|² (norm_add_sq_real). This uses ⟨ιv, ι'u⟩ = 0 and that ι, ι' preserve norms.
2. (Proof of (a).) For w ∈ ℝⁿ, Lw = ιw + ι'(Λw). If Lw = 0, step 1 gives 0 = |Lw|² = |w|² + |Λw|² ≥ |w|², so w = 0. Thus ker L = 0 and L is injective. Hence dim S = dim range L = dim ℝⁿ = n (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin).
3. (Nearest point.) For y ∈ ℝ^{n+k} and s ∈ S: |y − p_S y| ≤ |y − s|. Indeed |y − p_S y| = inf_{s' ∈ S}|y − s'| (Submodule.starProjection_minimal). That family of norms is bounded below by 0, so the infimum is at most its value at s (ciInf_le).
4. (Proof of (b).) Fix v ∈ ℝⁿ and w ∈ ℝᵏ. Since ξ cancels and ι' is linear, y = ξ + ιv + ι'w − (ξ + ι'c) = ιv + ι'(w − c).
 The vector s := Lv = ιv + ι'(Λv) lies in S. Also y − s = ι'(w − c) − ι'(Λv) = ι'(w − c − Λv), which has norm |w − c − Λv| because ι' is an isometry. By step 3, |y − p_S y| ≤ |w − c − Λv|.
 By step 1 with u := w − c, |y|² = |v|² + |w − c|² ≥ |v|². Both norms are nonnegative, so |v| ≤ |y|.
5. (range ι = T.) ι is an isometry, hence injective, so dim range ι = dim ℝⁿ = n = dim T. Also range ι ⊆ T by hypothesis. A subspace of the finite-dimensional space T with the same dimension equals T (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq). Hence range ι = T.
6. (range ι' = T^⊥.) Take w ∈ ℝᵏ and u ∈ T. By step 5, u = ιv for some v, so ⟨u, ι'w⟩ = ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0. Thus ι'w ∈ T^⊥ (Submodule.mem_orthogonal), i.e. range ι' ⊆ T^⊥.
 Next, dim T + dim T^⊥ = dim ℝ^{n+k} = n + k (Submodule.finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal), so dim T^⊥ = k. Since ι' is injective, dim range ι' = k. Hence range ι' = T^⊥ (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq).
7. (Proof of (c).) Fix x ∈ ℝ^{n+k} and put y₀ := x − ξ.
 Since p_T y₀ ∈ T = range ι (step 5), p_T y₀ = ιv for some v ∈ ℝⁿ.
 Since y₀ − p_T y₀ ∈ T^⊥ (Submodule.sub_starProjection_mem_orthogonal) and T^⊥ = range ι' (step 6), y₀ − p_T y₀ = ι'w for some w ∈ ℝᵏ. Moreover |w| = |ι'w| = |(x − ξ) − p_T(x − ξ)|.
 Then x = ξ + p_T y₀ + (y₀ − p_T y₀) = ξ + ιv + ι'w. So (b), applied to this v and w, reads: |(x − τ) − p_S(x − τ)| ≤ |w − c − Λv| and |v| ≤ |x − τ|.
 By the triangle inequality and |Λv| ≤ ‖Λ‖|v| (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm): |w − c − Λv| ≤ |w − c| + |Λv| ≤ |w| + |c| + ‖Λ‖|v|. Since ‖Λ‖ ≥ 0 and |v| ≤ |x − τ|, this is ≤ |w| + |c| + ‖Λ‖|x − τ|.
 Substituting |w| = |(x − ξ) − p_T(x − ξ)| gives (c). Together with steps 2 and 4 this proves (a), (b) and (c). ∎
proof_key_steps: Pythagoras: |ιv + ι'u|² = |v|² + |u|² by orthogonality and the isometry property.
L = ι + ι'∘Λ has |Lw|² ≥ |w|², so it is injective and dim S = n.
Nearest point: |y − p_S y| ≤ |y − s| for every s ∈ S (starProjection_minimal).
(b): y = ιv + ι'(w − c) and y − Lv = ι'(w − c − Λv), so |y − p_S y| ≤ |w − c − Λv|; Pythagoras gives |v| ≤ |y|.
Dimension count: range ι = T and range ι' = T^⊥.
(c): write x − ξ = ιv + ι'w with |w| = |(x − ξ) − p_T(x − ξ)|, apply (b), then the triangle and operator-norm inequalities with |v| ≤ |x − τ|.

audit.reason: The prose and one-line proposition match all hypotheses and three conclusions, including zero-dimensional cases. Pythagoras proves injectivity, dimension and the coordinate bound; projection minimality proves the graph-distance bound. Equal-dimension inclusions identify both frame ranges, allowing the orthogonal decomposition and operator-norm estimate to prove the final bound. Every step is supplied and non-circular. Finite-dimensional projection instances elaborate correctly.
